action: Operators of solar, storage and thermal plants: confirm remote access paths and telecontrol are monitored and that incident-reporting steps under Chile's Law 21.663 are rehearsed.
date_note: Date of the reporting; the Coordinador recorded the forced disconnection on 27 August 2026 and the plant was still offline in its 14 November report.
exec: A 103 MW solar plant and its battery system have been offline for almost three months after a recorded cyberattack, with no cause or restart date public.
plain: A large solar plant and battery system in northern Chile have been disconnected from the power grid since late August after a cyberattack. Almost three months on, the cause and restart date are not public.
summary: Chile's Coordinador Eléctrico Nacional recorded the forced disconnection of the 103 MW Huatacondo solar plant and its 98 MW/312 MWh battery system on 27 August with the cause 'cyberattack', and its 14 November report still showed both at 0% availability. The Coordinador says it activated disconnection protocols after the company reported the event. On 11 November a deputy asked the security and energy ministries for details. No technical cause or reconnection date has been published.
title: Chile's Huatacondo solar plant still offline almost three months after cyberattack

validation.note: pv magazine Latinoamérica (16 Nov) and Actualidad Jurídica DOE (18 Nov) read; both rely on the Coordinador's records and statements. The Coordinador's own report was not read. A Turkish site (DonanımHaber) repeats it. No technical details or attribution are public.
